$ openssl x509 -in pay-edge.pem.crt -outform DER | sha256sum
8a86ce9994efda613354233f9e7951a7bc193038f96265f596ce61292608ec72 *-
$ sha256sum pay-edge.der.crt
8a86ce9994efda613354233f9e7951a7bc193038f96265f596ce61292608ec72 *pay-edge.der.crt

$ openssl pkcs12 -in gateway.p12 -clcerts -nokeys -passin pass:changeit -out gateway-from-p12.pem.crt
$ sha256sum gateway-from-p12.pem.crt
a98c76f0ef880829f8c8eaf29f25bc8eef5f896c77961c451dc6db1ff8f39eb5 *gateway-from-p12.pem.crt
   -- NOTE: this raw PEM-text hash does NOT match the original cert.pem's PEM
      hash, because openssl pkcs12 -clcerts prepends "Bag Attributes"/
      "subject="/"issuer=" comment lines before the PEM block. This is the
      exact non-canonical-PEM trap Lock sec.6 TOPO-X3 / harness T6 warns about:
      hashing the raw PEM bytes as extracted is NOT reliable identity.

$ diff <(openssl x509 -in ../../../../../../../ecdat-harness/harness/build/out/gateway-p12/cert.pem) gateway-from-p12.pem.crt
0a1,5
> Bag Attributes
>     localKeyID: CD 4A C4 A6 28 53 B8 65 6E 9D 2F 8A E3 AE 8E F0 37 42 19 5D
>     friendlyName: payment-gateway
> subject=O=Harness Payments, CN=payment-gateway
> issuer=O=Harness Intermediate CA (ECC), CN=Harness Intermediate CA ECC

$ sha256sum gateway-from-p12.der.crt
7c93c6a1fcf48e98b1bb1cc6ee177e7c0fa046cd34a405c8449710c73cb62998 *gateway-from-p12.der.crt
$ openssl x509 -in <original cert.pem> -outform DER | sha256sum
7c93c6a1fcf48e98b1bb1cc6ee177e7c0fa046cd34a405c8449710c73cb62998 *-

CONCLUSION: once every encoding is canonicalized to DER via `openssl x509
-outform DER` (running the PKCS12-extracted cert back through the x509
command strips the Bag Attributes header and re-emits pure DER-then-PEM),
SHA-256 over the DER bytes is identical across the PEM source file, the
independently-produced DER file, and the cert extracted from the PKCS12
keystore. It is NOT identical if you hash the raw text openssl pkcs12
emits directly, because that text is not canonical PEM (comment lines are
part of the file). This supports Lock sec.15.2 T6's "canonicalised first"
qualifier -- canonicalization is not a formality, it's load-bearing.
